Subject: Pilot extension — phased commit + ops-credit ladder (SkyBridge)

Hi Ethan / Alicia,

Thanks again for the time this week — team enjoyed walking through the inference latency and safety checks. Based on our usage telemetry (attached) and the product goals you shared, we put together two practical ways to bridge the remaining runway while preserving your evaluation velocity and procurement constraints:

Option A — Short extension + straight credit
- 14-day extension to your existing pilot window
- $7,500 one-time credit applied to usage (tokens/embeddings)
- No change to current SSO/KMS setup

Option B — Phased commit + ops-credit ladder (preferred for teams who want engineering support)
- 30-day extension tied to a 3-stage milestone plan:
  * Milestone 1 (week 2): integration validation -> 300 ops credits + 5% usage discount
  * Milestone 2 (week 4): throughput test -> 400 ops credits + additional 5% (10% total)
  * Milestone 3 (end of month): production smoke -> 300 ops credits + exec review and conversion playbook
- Ops credits redeemable for engineering time (up to 8-hour increments) or applied to invoice as offset for usage overage.
- Billing: split invoice — 50% on amendment execution, remainder net 30 after Milestone 2 completion (flexible per procurement request).

Attachments: pilot-usage-report.csv, proposed-amendment-draft.pdf (simple amendment, no product-level SLA changes).

Two quick clarifications we need from you to finalize:
1) Do you prefer credits as bill offsets or as reserved engineering hours?
2) Any PO or specific procurement wording we should bake into the amendment (e.g., net-45, tax clauses)?

If it helps, Marissa can run a 20-minute pricing walkthrough tomorrow and we can drop in legal to confirm amendment language.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

- We lean toward Option B (ops credits) because our engineering team needs dedicated time to validate the throughput plan. Can credits be used for both 1:1 engineering time and token offsets?
- Procurement note: our finance team prefers an invoice/PO flow (net-30); legal will want a simple amendment that references the existing MSA.

Also, can you confirm whether the milestone credits expire if we don't schedule the engineering sessions within 60 days? Our vendor governance requires expiration windows.

If you and Marissa can do a 20-minute call tomorrow at 10am PT, Alicia and I will be on.

Hey Ethan — glad Option B looks like the right path. Confirming details so procurement and engineering have a clean handoff: 

1) Credits behavior (short):
- Ops credits are fungible: can be redeemed for Redwood engineering time (we book discrete sessions) or automatically applied as dollar offsets on overage charges. You choose per-credit redemption.
- Expiry: standard 90-day expiration from amendment execution; we can shorten to 60 days in the amendment if your governance requires it.

2) Milestone trigger mechanics:
- Milestone completion is self-attested by SkyBridge via a short form + a quick triage call with our eng lead (David). Credits for the milestone will be applied within 5 business days after completion confirmation.

3) Billing/procurement:
- We can accept PO + net-30 invoice (no problem).
- Initial invoice would be for the committed tranche (50% on amendment signature).

4) Escrow / legal: amendment references the current MSA and does not change data residency or KMS clauses. We’ll include a one-line clause for credit expiry and redemption mechanics.

If that all sounds good we’ll: (a) shorten expiry to 60 days in the draft, (b) add PO/net-30 language, and (c) send a DocuSign-ready amendment and a one-page milestone checklist.

Naomi or I can take the 10am PT slot tomorrow. David — can you join for the 10–10:20 window to answer any technical Milestone questions?

Thanks —
